source.label: SIPRI: Trends in international arms transfers, 2025 (March 2026)

arms.note: SIPRI covers deliveries of major conventional weapons. Small arms, ammunition and most aid packages' smaller items are not counted.

blocs.name: North Atlantic Treaty Organization
blocs.what: Military alliance whose members pledge, under Article 5, to treat an attack on one as an attack on all.

blocs.name: US bilateral defence treaties in Asia and the Pacific
blocs.what: Countries with a mutual defence treaty with the United States outside NATO: Japan (1960), South Korea (1953), the Philippines (1951), Australia (ANZUS, 1951) and Thailand (1954).

sources.label: US State Department: US collective defense arrangements

blocs.name: AUKUS
blocs.what: Security pact under which the US and UK are helping Australia acquire nuclear-powered submarines and share advanced military technology.

blocs.name: Five Eyes
blocs.what: Intelligence-sharing alliance dating from the Second World War.

blocs.name: Quadrilateral Security Dialogue
blocs.what: Diplomatic and security partnership of four Indo-Pacific democracies, widely seen as a counterweight to China. Not a defence pact.

blocs.name: Collective Security Treaty Organization
blocs.what: Russian-led military alliance of former Soviet states with a mutual defence clause.

status.ARM: froze its participation in 2024 and says it will leave

sources.label: Armenpress: Armenia's CSTO membership expected to remain frozen (2026)

blocs.name: Russia and North Korea defence treaty
blocs.what: The 2024 Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty commits each to help the other if attacked. North Korean troops fought for Russia in Kursk.

sources.label: Wikipedia: North Korea and Russia relations

blocs.name: China and North Korea treaty of friendship
blocs.what: The 1961 treaty of friendship, cooperation and mutual assistance, China's only formal defence treaty.

sources.label: Council on Foreign Relations: The China-North Korea relationship

blocs.name: Saudi Arabia and Pakistan defence agreement
blocs.what: Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025: aggression against one is treated as aggression against both.

blocs.name: Alliance of Sahel States
blocs.what: Confederation formed in 2024 by the military governments of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger after they left ECOWAS, with a mutual defence pact and a joint force.

blocs.name: European Union
blocs.what: Political and economic union with a single market, shared laws, and for most members the euro. It also has a mutual assistance clause.

blocs.name: African Union
blocs.what: Union of all 55 African states (including Western Sahara, not shown here). Members that have had coups are often suspended until civilian rule returns.
blocs.note: Several members are suspended at any given time after coups (in 2026 these included Sudan, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger and Guinea-Bissau). Suspended members are still listed.

sources.label: Arab News: African Union suspends Guinea-Bissau after military coup

blocs.name: Arab League
blocs.what: Organisation of 22 Arab states. Syria was readmitted in 2023 after a 12-year suspension.

blocs.name: Gulf Cooperation Council
blocs.what: Political and economic alliance of the six Gulf monarchies.

blocs.name: Association of Southeast Asian Nations
blocs.what: Regional bloc of Southeast Asian states. Timor-Leste became its 11th member in October 2025.

blocs.name: Economic Community of West African States
blocs.what: West African bloc with free movement and a regional court. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger left in January 2025.

blocs.name: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
blocs.what: Eurasian security and economic forum led by China and Russia. Belarus joined in 2024.

blocs.name: BRICS
blocs.what: Group of large emerging economies pitched as an alternative to Western-led institutions. Saudi Arabia was invited in 2023 but has not confirmed membership.

blocs.name: Eurasian Economic Union
blocs.what: Russian-led single market and customs union of former Soviet states.

blocs.name: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
blocs.what: Oil producers' cartel that sets output targets. The UAE left on 1 May 2026, after Angola in 2024.

sources.label: Enerdata: UAE announces exit from OPEC effective 1 May 2026

blocs.name: Mercosur
blocs.what: South American trade bloc. Bolivia became a full member in 2024; Venezuela has been suspended since 2016.

blocs.name: United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement
blocs.what: North American free trade agreement that replaced NAFTA in 2020, up for joint review in 2026.

sources.label: Office of the US Trade Representative: USMCA

blocs.name: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
blocs.what: Pacific Rim free trade agreement. The UK joined in December 2024; Costa Rica's accession talks concluded in 2026.

sources.label: New Zealand Foreign Ministry: CPTPP accession

blocs.name: Group of Seven
blocs.what: Forum of seven large industrial democracies; the EU also takes part.
